issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired land may be assessed by belts reflecting differences in land quality rather than at a uniform rate when the record does not support uniform valuation.
material_facts: Approximately 331 acres were acquired for a residential-cum-commercial complex.
The Collector divided the land into three belts, and the courts below maintained or revised the belting while setting different rates for the belts.
The claimants argued that the land’s intended building use and its location alongside a major road warranted uniform compensation.
The Court considered the land’s differing quality and the absence of supporting material for uniform valuation.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to discard the belting system or apply a uniform rate, finding no basis in the record to interfere with the High Court’s assessment.
issues.legal_principle: In determining compensation for acquired land, the land’s quality and productive characteristics may be considered even when it is acquired for building purposes. A claim for uniform valuation must have supporting material in the record. No provision or earlier case was cited for this reasoning.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and acquired_land_has_quality_differences and not record_supports_uniform_valuation

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking increased compensation for acquired land.
predicates.acquired_land_has_quality_differences: The acquired land varies in quality or productive characteristics.
predicates.record_supports_uniform_valuation: The record contains material supporting assessment of all the acquired land at a uniform rate.

issues.definition: When an appeal seeks increased compensation for acquired land that varies in quality and the record does not support a uniform rate, the land may remain assessed in belts.

issues.legal_issue: A sale of a small, fully constructed parcel does not by itself establish the value of a much larger acquired tract when the parcel’s characteristics differ materially.
material_facts: The claimants relied on a pre-acquisition purchase of approximately 125 square yards at Rs. 42 per square yard as an indication of the value of the acquired land.
The cited parcel was small and had a house and a godown facing the major road.
The High Court rejected the comparison, and the Supreme Court considered that reasoning sound.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the small parcel sale as a basis for increasing compensation for the acquired land.
issues.legal_principle: A sale instance must be assessed in light of the size and characteristics of the parcel and its comparability to the acquired land. The Court relied on the parcel’s small area and its existing construction and road frontage. No provision or earlier case was cited for this reasoning.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and comparator_sale_relied_on and comparator_parcel_is_small and comparator_parcel_is_fully_constructed

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking increased compensation for acquired land.
predicates.comparator_sale_relied_on: A party relies on a sale of another parcel as evidence of the acquired land’s value.
predicates.comparator_parcel_is_small: The parcel used for comparison is small in area relative to the acquired tract.
predicates.comparator_parcel_is_fully_constructed: The comparison parcel has substantial existing construction.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, a sale of a small, fully constructed parcel relied on as a comparison does not establish the value of the acquired land.

issues.legal_issue: A judgment from another acquisition case cannot support an increased compensation claim when it has not been placed on the record as evidence and no permission to adduce additional evidence has been sought.
material_facts: The claimants argued that another judgment concerning land acquired under the same notification had relied on the sale instance and awarded Rs. 42 per square yard.
That other judgment had not been brought on the record as evidence in these proceedings.
The claimants had not sought permission to adduce additional evidence.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the argument based on the other judgment and held that it could not be used to support the requested rate.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment from another case that has not been brought on the record as evidence cannot be used to support the requested valuation in the proceeding; the Court also noted that no permission to adduce additional evidence had been sought. No provision or earlier case was cited for this reasoning.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and another_case_judgment_relied_on and judgment_not_in_record and no_permission_for_additional_evidence_sought

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking increased compensation for acquired land.
predicates.another_case_judgment_relied_on: A party relies on a judgment from another case to support a higher valuation.
predicates.judgment_not_in_record: The other case’s judgment has not been placed on the record as evidence in the proceeding.
predicates.no_permission_for_additional_evidence_so: The party has not sought permission to introduce the judgment as additional evidence.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, a party cannot use another case’s judgment to support higher compensation when that judgment is absent from the record and permission to introduce additional evidence has not been sought.
